metadata.notes: No duplicate adjacent weather histories promoted; two alternate IDs retained per date.

reviews.title_after: Blizzard of 2016 buries New York City in near-whiteout conditions
reviews.location_after: New York City and the northeastern United States
reviews.core_fact: Blizzard conditions swept New York City and nearby areas on January 23, 2016, within a January 22–24 nor'easter.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS weather reports and NASA contemporaneous satellite imagery corroborate the storm; NASA may reuse NWS ground amounts.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Storm-total snowfall spans January 22–24; do not attribute whole-storm accumulation to January 23.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original blizzard swath map from dated station and satellite observations

reviews.title_before: Winter Storm — W SALT LAKE T X W/E TOOLE T X E, Utah
reviews.title_after: The Ash Wednesday Storm devastates the Mid-Atlantic shoreline
reviews.core_fact: A prolonged extratropical nor'easter produced devastating Mid-Atlantic coastal flooding March 7, 1962 during a multi-day storm.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS coastal history, NPS history and NOAA gauge archive corroborate dates but share underlying historical research.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Storm spanned March 5–8 and several high tides; not a tropical hurricane. Distinguish date of worst damage from storm initiation.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original five-high-tide timeline and coastal water-level transect

reviews.title_after: Weeks of heavy rain precede the Oso landslide in Washington
reviews.core_fact: The destructive Oso landslide occurred on March 22, 2014 after unusually wet conditions in northwest Washington.
reviews.source_dependence: USGS hydroclimate research and NASA satellite analysis corroborate occurrence; some geologic interpretations overlap.
reviews.unverified_cautions: The landslide occurred in fair weather after antecedent wet weeks. Rainfall was a contributing factor alongside geology and groundwater; do not claim a March 22 thunderstorm caused it.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original antecedent rainfall anomaly and slope/river schematic

reviews.title_before: Heavy Snow — SAN DIEGO COUNTY MOUNTAINS, California
reviews.title_after: TIROS-1 launches the era of weather observation from orbit
reviews.core_fact: NASA launched TIROS-1 on April 1, 1960, pioneering dedicated satellite observation of cloud patterns.
reviews.source_dependence: NASA mission and NOAA/NESDIS/DARPA histories confirm launch date, with overlapping mission-record provenance.
reviews.unverified_cautions: TIROS-1 was the first successful dedicated weather satellite, not the first artificial satellite or the first orbital photograph of Earth.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original TIROS-1 orbit diagram and first-image timeline

reviews.title_before: Excessive Heat — LAS VEGAS VALLEY, Nevada
reviews.title_after: Grand Island's Night of the Twisters sends seven tornadoes across Nebraska
reviews.location_after: Grand Island and Hall County, Nebraska
reviews.core_fact: Seven tornadoes affected Grand Island and its vicinity on June 3, 1980, several with unusual paths.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS survey retrospective and Nebraska State Historical Society separately confirm event/date; path geometry shares survey data.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Do not merge separate tornado tracks, casualties or survey ratings; historical F-scale classifications are not EF-scale.

reviews.title_after: Elie, Manitoba is struck by Canada's first documented F5 tornado
reviews.core_fact: A tornado struck Elie, Manitoba on June 22, 2007 and was eventually rated F5, Canada's first documented F5.
reviews.source_dependence: Provincial hazard history and UW-CIMSS dated satellite images independently support date/occurrence; final rating from Environment Canada survey.
reviews.unverified_cautions: June 25 provincial reports initially called F4; F5 was a later reassessment. Not EF5; intensity comes from damage survey, not GOES satellite.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original Elie path and GOES convection time series

reviews.title_after: The United Kingdom exceeds 40°C for the first time on record
reviews.core_fact: The Met Office verified 40.3°C at Coningsby on July 19, 2022, the UK's first observed reading above 40°C.
reviews.source_dependence: Met Office observation/QC and peer-reviewed RMetS evaluation agree, but the paper uses the same observational archive.
reviews.unverified_cautions: 40.3°C was a station maximum at Coningsby, not every part of the UK; station measurement and later QC supersede preliminary press estimates.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original UK station maximum-temperature map and historical threshold chart

reviews.title_after: Fog shrouds Manhattan as an Army B-25 strikes the Empire State Building
reviews.core_fact: A U.S. Army B-25 crashed into the Empire State Building on July 28, 1945 while fog and low cloud reduced visibility.
reviews.source_dependence: Municipal archives and Smithsonian corroborate date/weather; both partly draw on contemporary press accounts.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Fog was an operating condition, not a definitive single-cause finding. Avoid sensational casualty descriptions or reusing rights-uncleared photographs.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original 1945 Manhattan visibility and flight-routing cross-section

reviews.title_after: A thunderstorm microburst brings down Delta Flight 191 at DFW
reviews.core_fact: The NTSB determined that Delta Flight 191 encountered a microburst during approach to DFW on August 2, 1985.
reviews.source_dependence: NTSB investigated original flight/weather evidence; FAA and NWS interpret same investigation and broader wind-shear literature.
reviews.unverified_cautions: FAA educational discussion is based on NTSB investigation and not an independent second measurement. Separate later TDWR adoption from a single event's direct causal role.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original annotated microburst downdraft with flight path and wind vectors

reviews.title_after: Record rain swamps Columbia during South Carolina's historic flood
reviews.location_after: Columbia and the central South Carolina Midlands
reviews.core_fact: Torrential rainfall and severe flooding occurred around Columbia on October 4, 2015, with a USGS Congaree River crest that day.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS meteorological reports and USGS independent streamgage observations measure different parts of the same event.
reviews.unverified_cautions: KCAE 6.71 inches is Oct4 daily rainfall; 10.28 inches is Oct3–4 total. River peak flow/stage is distinct from rainfall or a universal statewide maximum.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original station precipitation vs Congaree peak hydrograph

reviews.title_after: A rare December derecho and tornado outbreak sweeps Iowa
reviews.location_after: Iowa and adjacent Upper Midwest states
reviews.core_fact: A December derecho and numerous tornadoes swept Iowa and neighboring states on December 15, 2021.
reviews.source_dependence: NWS surveys and Purdue MRCC summary corroborate the date but share NWS damage-report datasets.
reviews.unverified_cautions: Keep derecho thunderstorm gusts separate from synoptic pressure-gradient winds and from embedded tornado paths; preliminary and final tornado counts differ.
reviews.graphic_concept: Original temperature anomaly/derecho swath and surveyed tornado-track map
